paper.title: A global analysis of ${\bar B}\to DP$ and ${\bar B} \to {\bar D} P$ decays
paper.summary: Recently, a fit to the 15 measured branching ratios of ${\bar B} \to D P$ decays ($B = \{B^+, B^0, B_s^0\}$, $D = \{D^0, D^+, D_s^+\}$, $P \in \{π, K\}$) was performed under the assumption of flavor SU(3) symmetry [SU(3)$_F$]. A terrible fit was found: there was a $> 5σ$ disagreement with the SU(3)$_F$ limit of the Standard Model [SM$_{\rm{SU(3)}_F}$]. It was also found that this discrepancy can be removed by adding $\sim 20\%$ SU(3)$_F$-breaking effects. Now, the ${\bar B} \to D^0 P$ amplitudes can contribute to other observables (direct and indirect CP asymmetries) if they interfere with the amplitudes for ${\bar B} \to {\bar D}^0 P$ decays. paper.title: Can Learning to Answer Spatial Questions Improve Novel-View Generation?
paper.summary: Generating novel views from limited observations requires preserving both the appearance and spatial structure of a scene. Although recent approaches exploit fine-grained geometric cues, they do not explicitly model high-level semantic and spatial properties such as object identity, attributes, and inter-object relationships. In this work, we investigate whether 3D language understanding can provide complementary supervision for novel-view generation. We introduce Ask4NV, built on a pretrained unified multimodal model with a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture. Our model incorporates camera geometry into both VAE and ViT representations and leverages understanding features during generation through joint self-attention with a modality-aware attention masking strategy. paper.title: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving
paper.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are gaining attention in autonomous driving, inheriting commonsense priors from large language models (LLMs) and widening the navigation interface from a fixed command set to free-form natural-language instructions. However, this open-ended interface exposes a new vulnerability surface: an inattentive driver may issue instructions that are unsafe given the current scene, and a malicious user may issue dangerous ones on purpose. We present the first benchmark suite that evaluates navigation following and conflict awareness together, along with adversarial robustness. paper.title: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion
paper.summary: Recent advances in robot learning have driven rapid progress in humanoid control, enabling increasingly agile behaviors in the real world. However, humanoid control networks are typically obtained through conventional training procedures, while comparatively little attention has been given to directly modeling the distribution of their learned weights and generating functional networks in weight space. In this work, we investigate whether high-performing humanoid control networks can be generatively modeled directly through their weights. We adopt a latent diffusion framework that couples a linear autoencoder with a Diffusion Transformer. The autoencoder compresses actor network parameters into a compact latent space, and the Diffusion Transformer models the distribution of these latents.

paper.title: VITAL: From Visual Motion to Precise Action
paper.summary: World-action models aim to turn visual anticipation into driving decisions, yet typically train action experts on trajectory representations defined independently of visual dynamics. This motivates deriving action targets directly from visual motion. We first examine a simpler setting in which trajectories are reconstructed from recorded future images. Even without the need for future prediction, reconstruction captures the dominant maneuver but leaves centimeter-scale errors. We therefore introduce VITAL (Vision-Induced Tokens for Action Learning), an action tokenizer that couples a visually derived motion scaffold with a compact residual encoding the trajectory error left by that scaffold.
